authoring.question: q-328086
authoring.value:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{ST},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/cd8dc0d2e01927c8b2ca116265b257d835a1baae62272b703610f2947d92a8c2.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QS}=-b,\,\overset{\to }{ST}=-c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/8ed8c71e0d45ae0c9cf7d8a7d2889ee3a79471aaeb408ad0f53f487523daac13.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{ST} \\  & =-b+(-c) \\  & =-b-c.\end{aligned}
$$

authoring.value:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $Q$ consisting only of the vectors $\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c,$ and $\mathbf d.$

According to the triangle law of addition, 

$$
{\color{red}{\overrightarrow{TQ}}} = {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{TS}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{SQ}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/4902397acd28e2e5f85063ba55c576d3768360225a705f31a66bd460405dd5a6.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TS}} = \mathbf{d}, \qquad {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{SQ}}} = -\mathbf{b}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/08086f7e09568f908aa4919a1156d52e465216221be8908e72a1fd90ec8843dd.png)

  

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TQ} & =\overset{\to }{TS}+\overset{\to }{SQ} \\  & =d+(-b) \\  & =d-b.\end{aligned}
$$

authoring.value:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $S$ consisting only of the vectors $\mathbf a, \mathbf b,$ or $\mathbf c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
{\color{red}{\overrightarrow{TS}}} = {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{TP}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{PQ}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{QS}}}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/53940607b5cbf0220008e6e31ec60f2fd7fd2e4f70c5a8e95e7fcfd64064b095.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TP}} = -\mathbf{b}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{PQ}} = \mathbf{a}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{QS}} = \mathbf{c}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/810cce10eb330b1767a101d9107a9534c437daa123f13056a486a9fc96dbab89.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TS} & =\overset{\to }{TP}+\overset{\to }{PQ}+\overset{\to }{QS} \\  & =-b+a+c \\  & =a-b+c.\end{aligned}
$$
